result.summary: Enables Bitcoin Core to run as isolated processes by adding IPC wrappers for node and wallet interfaces using Cap'n Proto and libmultiprocess. When built with multiprocess support, bitcoin-gui spawns bitcoin-node as a child process, and bitcoin-node spawns bitcoin-wallet, communicating across socketpairs instead of running in a shared address space. Also updates the libmultiprocess subtree, exposes stable and unstable Chain interfaces over IPC, and makes btcsignals slot destruction eager on disconnect.
result.problem: The node, wallet, and GUI components run within a single monolithic address space. A memory corruption vulnerability or crash in the GUI or wallet can compromise consensus validation or take down the entire node.
evidence: Description notes that running GUI, node, and wallet in separate processes allows 'relevant functionality isolated into different processes' so 'node, wallet, and GUI code run in separate address spaces for better isolation' (PR description and doc/multiprocess.md).

Commit de0617691a notes concrete failure mode resolved by btcsignals changes: 'in multiprocess bitcoin-gui, where node notification callbacks own IPC proxy objects: their deferred destruction kept bitcoin-node from exiting and hung interface_gui.py until timeout.'
result.scope_notes: Very large change containing an update to the src/ipc/libmultiprocess git subtree, multiple new Cap'n Proto interface definitions, and core utility changes in btcsignals and interfaces::Init.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased onto #29409, updated the libmultiprocess subtree with upstream changes including platform compatibility fixes, introduced stable and unstable Chain IPC capnp wrappers, added an atomic_shared_ptr fallback in btcsignals for C++20 standard library variants lacking __cpp_lib_atomic_shared_ptr, and adjusted WalletLoader::restoreWallet parameter ordering.
result.card: Adds multiprocess capability to Bitcoin Core, allowing bitcoin-gui, bitcoin-node, and bitcoin-wallet to run as separate isolated executables communicating via Cap'n Proto IPC over socketpairs. Currently, all components share a single address space, meaning a crash or vulnerability in wallet or GUI code can compromise the validating node. This PR represents the core implementation of the process separation project (#28722). It is based on #29409 and enables followup PRs #19460 and #19461.

risk.why: A flaw in btcsignals callback destruction or IPC proxy synchronization could lead to deadlocks, use-after-free crashes, or hanging process terminations during node shutdown.
